promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 10 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: Your knee comes first this week. That means no tempo, no long run and a physio check, plus two short flat test runs only once stairs stop hurting. You are 10 weeks out, so one quiet week leaves room for the 3:45 goal.

flags.title: Long run cut short
flags.detail: You planned 13 mi, stopped at 8.5 mi and walked home. Stopping was right, and there is no long run this week.

flags.title: Stairs and walking
flags.detail: Check the knee every morning. Run only after 48 hours with no pain on stairs or when walking.

flags.title: Pain during a run
flags.detail: Any knee pain on Thursday or Saturday means stop and walk home. Do not push through it.

flags.title: Flat routes only
flags.detail: The pain started on a hill and turned sharp on downhills. Avoid both until the knee settles.

flags.title: Physio appointment
flags.detail: Book it this week. If their advice differs from the plan, follow their advice.

answers.question: Is this an IT band thing? Should I still do Wednesday's tempo?
answers.answer:
I can't tell you whether it is the IT band, and guessing could steer you wrong. The pain is on the outside of the knee, grew during the week, turned sharp on downhills and now aches on stairs. A physio or sports doctor should look at that, so book an appointment this week.

No, skip Wednesday's tempo. Wednesday is easy cross-training instead. Faster running comes back only after several pain-free easy runs and once the physio is happy, so expect at least one more week without it.

new.analysis:
**The week went to plan until Sunday.** You ran the planned distances on Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Saturday. You judged the tempo well: 4 mi at about 7:59/mi against an 8:00 target, effort 7/10, with no pain.

**Stopping Sunday's long run early was the right call.** You planned 13 mi, stopped at 8.5 mi and walked home, so the week ended at 32 mi instead of about 36 mi. Pushing on through sharp pain on the downhills would likely have cost you far more than four miles.

**How the knee changed over the week matters more than any single day.** It went from mild tightness to sharp pain in four days. Now it hurts off the run too.

| When | Pain | What you noted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Thu Aug 13 | 2/10 | Tight on the last hill |
| Sat Aug 15 | 1/10 | Tight before, fine during |
| Sun Aug 16 | 4/10 | Sharp on downhills from mile 7 |
| After the long run | not rated | Aches going down stairs |

**This week is built to let the knee settle.** Running is limited to two short flat runs, at most 6 mi in total. Each one happens only if stairs and walking have been pain-free. Cross-training fills the other days, so your aerobic fitness holds while the pounding drops.

**A lighter week was due anyway.** This is the fourth week of the build, after 30, 32, 35 and 32 mi, so stepping back fits the pattern. Your fitness is in good shape: easy runs average 9:50/mi at 138 bpm, slightly better than three weeks ago.

**One quiet week does not end the 3:45 goal.** A few days of cross-training cost very little fitness. Running on a knee that keeps getting worse could cost several weeks, and that is the real threat to race day.

**What comes next depends on the knee.** If both test runs are pain-free and the physio agrees, the week of Aug 24 brings back easy runs and a shorter long run on flat ground. After that come hills and the tempo, and the long run restarts below 13 mi.

safetyCallouts.title: Get your right knee checked.
safetyCallouts.body: The pain grew during the week, turned sharp on downhills and now aches on stairs, so see a physio or sports doctor this week and follow their advice.

safetyCallouts.title: Stop running if it gets worse.
safetyCallouts.body: If the knee hurts more each day, swells, locks, gives way or wakes you at night, stop running and get it seen promptly.
